arm: S5b log-log LMR (retest of the arm shelved 2026-08-07)

why_it_was_retested.shelved_note: S5 was shelved after two retunes with the read: 'with TT-first ordering fixed (S1), late-move index is a weak pruning signal at depth ~7/150ms; revisit after S8 continuation history / staged movegen improve ordering'. See evidence/search_arms/s5_lmr_shelved.json.
two_things_changed: H1 (history rewrite) and H4 (winning-capture priority) fixed move ordering on 2026-08-16. That is the precondition the shelving note named: late-move index only carries information if the move list is ordered well enough for lateness to mean anything.

The 150 ms A/B harness was shown to UNDERSTATE depth-dependent changes by ~2.3x (H1+H4: +38.3 at 150 ms vs +88.7 at 1000 ms). S5 was judged at 150 ms on a schedule whose whole effect is extra depth, so it was measured by an instrument that could not see it.

change.before: Flat reduction of 1 whenever depth >= 3, idx >= 3, not a check, not a capture. The 4th move and the 40th were reduced identically.
change.after: r = clamp(ln(depth) * ln(idx) / 2.25, 1, depth - 2), same gating.
change.divisor: 2.25, carried over from the S5 v2 retune rather than re-tuned. Retuning it is untested headroom.
change.site: PieBot/src/search/alphabeta.rs, extracted as Searcher::lmr_reduction so it is unit-testable
change.unchanged: The existing full-depth verification re-search on a reduced fail-high is retained.

tests: always_leaves_the_child_at_least_one_ply (r <= depth - 2, so a reduced search cannot collapse into qsearch)
actually_exceeds_the_flat_reduction_it_replaces (guards against the change being a silent no-op)

prescreen_matein3.note: matein3 cannot measure NPS -- it loads from FEN with a ~1-entry history -- but node count plus mates-solved is a ~4 s test of whether the tree changed at all.

measurements.harness: compare_play, 1000 ms/move, --paired-openings, --noise-plies 12 --noise-topk 5, 11 workers, one search thread per engine
measurements.time_control_rationale: 1000 ms, not 150 ms, per the corrected protocol for depth-dependent arms.
measurements.screen_did_not_overstate: Screen +22.6, confirmation +22.3. Unlike H1 (+27.0 screened, +18.1 confirmed). Worth noting because the standing expectation is that screens overstate; this one did not, so the rule is a tendency rather than a correction to apply.
measurements.bootstrap_method: 20,000 resamples over the 500 opening PAIRS, not over games. Pairing is what moves the lower bound from +6.9 to +12.2 at n=1000.

mechanism: The gain is depth, bought at equal NPS: +0.85 ply for a 15% node reduction on the mate suite. A flat reduction spends the same effort on the 40th move as on the 4th; a log-log schedule reduces late moves harder while staying gentle where ordering is most likely to be right. This only pays once ordering is trustworthy, which is exactly what the 2026-08-07 shelving note predicted.

node_signatures.reminder: accept and accept_temp use different option sets (opts=alphabeta vs opts=(default)) and are NOT comparable to each other. Compare each against its own history.

caveats: Measured at 1000 ms on a 12-core Apple Silicon Mac, single search thread per engine. CCRL 40/15 is 22.5 s/move; the arm should gain more there if the depth-dependence holds, but that is an extrapolation.
The 2.25 divisor is inherited, not tuned. A sweep is untested headroom.

Interaction with the Lazy SMP change promoted earlier the same day is untested: both were measured against a single-threaded baseline, and reductions that pay at one search width may behave differently when helpers are filling the TT.
queue_implication: Two of the four arms rejected at 150 ms have now been re-tested at 1000 ms and one promoted. Still outstanding on the same reasoning: H2 continuation history (+2.6 at 150 ms), history-modulated LMR (+3.5), and LMP (~1% nodes, lost a mate when pushed).
